title: Secret manager accounts
intro: The accounts DBine uses to sign in to a secret manager, connected once on this computer and used by as many connections as you like. They are not exported, not synced and not included in backups; their secrets are in the system keychain.

wizard.title: Connect Zoho Vault
wizard.client_id_format: The Client ID doesn't have Zoho's format (1000.XXXX)
wizard.label: Account name

s1.title: Create your own client in Zoho
s1.intro: DBine signs in to Zoho Vault with an API client of your own, a «Self Client». It is created once, with your Zoho account.
s1.a: Sign in with your Zoho account and click «GET STARTED». If you already have clients, click «ADD CLIENT», at the top right.
s1.b: Go to «Self Client» and click «CREATE NOW»; then click «CREATE» and confirm with «OK». If you already have a Self Client, open it from the list.
s1.c: In the «Client Secret» tab, copy the «Client ID» and the «Client Secret» and paste them here:

s2.title: Generate a code
s2.a: In the same Self Client, open the «Generate Code» tab.
s2.c: In «Time Duration» choose «10 minutes» and in «Scope Description» type «DBine».
s2.d: Click «CREATE». If Zoho asks you to choose the application and the portal or organization, choose Zoho Vault and your organization, and click «CREATE» again.
s2.e: Copy the code Zoho shows and paste it here. It expires after the time you chose: continue right away.

s3.title: Connect
s3.intro: DBine exchanges the code for a read permission and finds your account's data center on its own. Nothing is saved until the last step.
s3.noUser: Zoho didn't report the user: enter a name for the account.

s4.title: Master passphrase
s4.intro: Zoho Vault encrypts secrets with your master passphrase and DBine decrypts them on this computer. It is checked now against your account.
s4.keychainHelp: It is saved in the system keychain, with the account.
s4.askHelp: It is checked now, but not saved: DBine asks for it the first time a connection needs it.
s4.commandHelp: DBine runs the command now to check it, and every time it needs it.
s4.doneHelp: «{{label}}» can now be chosen in connections that take their password from Zoho Vault.

server.title: Where is your Bitwarden account?
server.intro: Bitwarden cloud accounts live in the region where they were created.

apiKey.title: Your personal API key
apiKey.intro: DBine signs in to your vault with your personal API key. The vault stays encrypted: DBine decrypts it on this computer with your master password.
apiKey.a: In the Bitwarden web app, go to «Settings» → «Security» → «Keys».
apiKey.b: Click «View API key» and confirm with your master password.
apiKey.c: Copy the «client_id» and the «client_secret» and paste them here:
apiKey.note: The API key does not ask for two-step sign-in. If you rotate it in Bitwarden, reconnect the account.

master.title: Master password
master.intro: DBine uses it to open your user key. It is checked against your vault when you connect the account.

token.title: The access token of a machine account
token.intro: DBine reads Secrets Manager as a machine account, with its access token.
token.a: In Bitwarden, open Secrets Manager and choose «Machine accounts» in the navigation.
token.b: Choose the machine account and open the «Access tokens» tab.
token.c: Click «Create access token», set a «Name» (for example DBine), choose when it expires in «Expires» and confirm with «Create access token».
token.d: Copy the token (Bitwarden shows it only once) and paste it here:

server.title: Your Vault or OpenBao server
server.intro: The address with its port, as the CLI uses it (VAULT_ADDR).
server.note: The namespace is only needed with Vault Enterprise or HCP Vault; the CA, if Vault's certificate was signed by your own CA.

auth.title: How DBine signs in
auth.token: With a token: the one from «vault login» or one from «vault token create». Empty: DBine uses «VAULT_TOKEN» or «~/.vault-token» each time.
auth.login: With OIDC or user and password, sign in with «vault login -method=oidc» (or «-method=userpass») and leave the token empty.

server.title: Your Secret Server
server.intro: Secret Server on your network or Secret Server Cloud; with Delinea Platform, sign-in happens on your platform tenant.
server.modeServer: Sign in to Secret Server (a user or an application account)
server.modePlatform: Sign in to Delinea Platform (a service user)
server.note: DBine talks only to these addresses, over HTTPS.

user.title: User and password
user.intro: The account DBine uses to read the secrets: a read-only one is best.
user.platform: In Delinea Platform, the service user is created in «Access» → «Users» → «More» → «Add service user»; its name is the client ID and its password, the secret.

server.title: Your Conjur
server.intro: Conjur Open Source or Enterprise, or Conjur Cloud (https://<subdomain>.secretsmgr.cyberark.cloud/api), and the organization account.
server.note: The CA only if Conjur's certificate was signed by your own CA.

identity.title: DBine's host or user
identity.intro: DBine signs in with the API key of a host (host/<id>) or of a user. Conjur provides a host's key when you load the policy that creates it, or when an administrator rotates it.

server.title: Your Central Credential Provider
server.intro: The web service URL (AIMWebService) and the AppID that the CyberArk administrator defined for DBine.
server.note: The CA only if the server's certificate was signed by your own CA.

certificate.title: The client certificate
certificate.intro: If the provider authenticates the application with a certificate, choose its files; otherwise leave it empty.
certificate.note: DBine stores the file paths, never a copy of the key; the passphrase goes to the system keychain.

cli.title: The 1Password CLI
cli.intro: DBine reads 1Password with its CLI («op»), which keeps its own session: DBine stores nothing.
cli.none: The CLI has no accounts yet.
cli.a: In the 1Password app, go to «Settings» → «Developer» and turn on «Integrate with 1Password CLI».
cli.b: On Linux, first turn on «Settings» → «Security» → «Unlock using system authentication».
cli.c: Or add the account in the terminal with «op account add».

profile.title: Profile and region
profile.intro: DBine uses the AWS credentials of this computer, like the AWS CLI: it stores no keys.
profile.none: There are no profiles in ~/.aws: the default chain is used.
profile.note: Profiles come from ~/.aws/config and ~/.aws/credentials («aws configure», «aws configure sso»).

vault.title: Your Azure Key Vault
vault.intro: DBine asks for the token from the Azure CLI («az login»), the Azure Developer CLI or the managed identity: it stores no credentials.
vault.notFound: There is no Azure CLI session: run «az login».
vault.a: The URL is in the Azure portal, in the vault: «Overview» → «Vault URI».
vault.tenantPlaceholder: The current one from the Azure CLI
vault.perAccount: Each account stores its own tenant: you can have one account per vault or per tenant.

azure.signIn: Sign in to that tenant with {{command}} and try again.

project.title: Your Google Cloud project
project.intro: DBine asks for the token from gcloud («gcloud auth login») or from the application default credentials: it stores no credentials.
project.notFound: There is no gcloud session: run «gcloud auth login».
project.accountHelp: DBine always asks for this account's token, even if you later change gcloud's active account. Empty: whichever is active at the time.
project.unpinned: This account uses gcloud's active account, which can change: pick one to pin it.

gcp.signIn: Sign in to gcloud with that account using {{command}} and try again.

database.title: Your KeePass database
database.intro: The .kdbx file and, if it uses one, its key file. DBine reads it on this computer, with no external programs.

master.title: Master password
master.intro: It is checked now, by opening the database.

connect.title: Check and connect
connect.bitwarden: DBine signs in with the API key, syncs the vault and checks the master password by opening your user key. If anything fails, nothing is saved.
connect.bitwarden_sm: DBine authenticates with the machine account's token and lists the secrets it can read, without opening them. If anything fails, nothing is saved.
connect.vault: DBine signs in and looks up the token (auth/token/lookup-self): its name and its policies. An AppRole token is revoked right away. If anything fails, nothing is saved.
connect.delinea: DBine requests an access token and looks up the current user. If anything fails, nothing is saved.
connect.conjur: DBine authenticates with the API key and queries whoami. If anything fails, nothing is saved.
connect.ccp: The Central Credential Provider has no query that doesn't hand out a password: DBine checks the TLS connection with the client certificate, without sending the AppID. The AppID is tested with «Test» on a connection.
connect.onepassword: DBine runs «op whoami» with the chosen account; 1Password may ask you to authorize it.
connect.aws: DBine signs an STS call (GetCallerIdentity) with the profile's credentials and shows the identity.
connect.azure: DBine asks the Azure CLI for a Key Vault token and shows who it is for.
connect.gcp: DBine asks gcloud for a token and shows the account.
connect.keepass: DBine opens the database with the chosen key.
connect.labelHelp: Empty: DBine uses the manager's name and who signed in.
